title: A token bucket rate limiter (per tenant)
prompt:
You run an LLM API. Each tenant (customer org) gets a bucket. A bucket holds up to capacity tokens and refills continuously at refillPerSec tokens per second. A request costs cost tokens (1 per request, or the number of LLM tokens for a weighted limit). If the bucket has enough, take them and allow; otherwise deny and say how long to wait.

Part 1: new TokenBucket({ capacity, refillPerSec, now }). now() returns ms. The bucket starts full. tryRemove(cost = 1) returns:

  • { allowed: true, remaining } where remaining = Math.floor(tokens left), or
  • { allowed: false, remaining, retryAfterMs } where retryAfterMs = Math.ceil((cost - tokens) / refillPerSec * 1000). If cost > capacity the request can never succeed: retryAfterMs: Infinity.

Refill lazily: on each call, add elapsedMs / 1000 * refillPerSec tokens, never above capacity. A denied request takes nothing.

Part 2: new TenantLimiter(configFor, now) where configFor(tenantId) returns { capacity, refillPerSec }. check(tenantId, cost) lazily creates one bucket per tenant and returns that bucket's tryRemove(cost).

tests.name: starts full: allows a burst of capacity, then denies
refills over time at refillPerSec
never refills above capacity after a long idle period
denied requests report retryAfterMs and take nothing
weighted cost: an LLM call that uses 1,200 tokens
a cost larger than capacity can never succeed
TenantLimiter keeps tenants isolated with per-plan limits

hints: Remember the time of the last call (this.last). At the start of every tryRemove, add (now - last) / 1000 * refillPerSec tokens, cap at capacity, then set last = now.
When denied, the shortfall is cost - tokens. At refillPerSec tokens per second, that takes shortfall / refillPerSec seconds. Check cost > capacity first and return Infinity.
For TenantLimiter, keep a Map from tenantId to bucket. On a miss: new TokenBucket({ ...this.configFor(id), now: this.now }).
explain:
This is the algorithm behind most public API limits, including the token-bucket style limits LLM providers describe for requests per minute and tokens per minute. It allows short bursts (up to capacity) while holding the long-run average to refillPerSec, and it needs only two numbers per tenant: tokens and last-refill time. In a fleet of servers those two numbers live in Redis and the refill-and-take step runs as one atomic Lua script, so two servers can't both spend the last token.

In an interview: "Token bucket per tenant, keyed in Redis, checked at the API gateway. Two buckets for an LLM API: requests per minute and tokens per minute. When denied, return 429 with Retry-After set from the bucket's refill time."
